chunks: From Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) who said: Indeed, Allah the Exalted did not grant Satan authority over those who have faith.
But upon those who take him as their master/wali.
And his authority over them is only so that We may know who believes in the Hereafter.
ai.seo_question: What is the difference between Satan's authority over believers and non-believers according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: In *Kamal al-Din*, Shaykh al-Saduq records Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifying that Satan’s *slutān* (authority) is not coercive but conditional upon human choice, serving as a divine test to distinguish the steadfast from the heedless. This interpretation aligns with the Shia understanding of *taklif* (accountability), where free will allows believers to overcome Satan’s whispers through conscious adherence to divine guidance.
